edit.description: share a numeric --max parse between the `job run` arg-rewrite (cli.ts:596-627) and the `loop` block (cli.ts:815-826); validate in the job-run branch before rewriting cmd/rest, so a bad value exits 2 with the job-run usage line before jobRun() preflight (cli.ts:656-669) wakes phases[0]
extend the §5b 'real CLI' cases (near line 851) with a non-numeric/negative --max case on a hibernating job: exits 2, prints the job-run usage line, baton stays hibernating

summary: `job run <name> --max abc` wakes chain.phases[0] before the --max numeric check fails, printing the wrong (loop) usage message

tests.asserts: `flume job run <name> --max <non-numeric|negative>` on a hibernating job exits 2, output names `flume job run` usage (not `flume loop`), and the job's baton is still hibernating

acceptance: a bad --max value on `job run` exits 2 with the job-run usage line and performs no wake; existing `flume loop --max` behavior unchanged
notes: cli.ts:596-627 rewrites `job run` into `loop` without checking --max is numeric; the check only runs later in the `loop` block (cli.ts:815-826), after jobRun() preflight (cli.ts:656-669) already woke phases[0]. Share the numeric parse so job run validates first, per engineering.md "Loud or nothing" — a path must not proceed over an unresolved input.
